author: MT Newswires
title: Technology Sector Update for 08/24/2018: ANET, SPLK, ADSK, HPQ, SMCI, ICHR, BPY
text:
Shutterstock photo Top Tech Stocks
MSFT +0.58%
AAPL +0.42%
IBM +0.43%
CSCO +0.74%
GOOG +1.26%
Technology stocks continued to build its Friday advance, with the shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 adding nearly 1.0% this afternoon while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was climbing more than 1.4%.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
+ Arista Networks ( ANET ) rallied Friday, climbing more than 10%, after the cloud networking company was selected to replace GGP Inc ( GGP ) in the S&P 500 index, effective with the start of regular-session trading on Tuesday, August 28. In a related move, S&P Dow Jones Indices said it was replacing Super Micro Computer ( SMCI ) in the S&P SmallCap 600 index with rival chipmaker Ichor Holdings ( ICHR ) beginning on Monday, August 27. Super Micro Computer earlier this week was suspended from trading on the Nasdaq Capital Market exchange while it works to complete several recent quarterly and annual reports. GGP no longer will be publicly traded following its upcoming acquisition by Brookfield Property Partners LP ( BPY )
In other sector news:
+ Splunk (SPLK) surged Friday, climbing almost 9%, after the "big data" analytics company reported Q2 sales beating Wall Street expectations, issued sales guidance for the current quarter exceeding analyst projections and raised its FY18 revenue forecast above Street views.
+ Autodesk (ADSK) rolled to a nearly 8% gain on Friday after the automated design software firm swung to a non-GAAP Q2 profit of $0.19 per share, reversing an $0.11 per share net loss last year and beating the Capital IQ consensus by $0.03 per share. Revenue rose to $611.7 million from $501.8 million in the year-ago period, also surpassing the $600 million analyst mean.
- HP (HPQ) slid almost 4% on Friday after the company said it expects non-GAAP FY18 net income in a range of $2.00 to $2.03 per share, lagging the Capital IQ consenus by at least $0.01 per share. The weaker-than-expected forecast upstaged improved fiscal Q3 financial results, with the computer manufacturer reporting adjusted net income of $0.52 per share in the May-to-July period compared with $0.43 per share in the year-ago quarter while revenue rose 11.4% to $14.6 billion. Analysts, on average, had been expecting HP to earn $0.51 per share on $14.29 billion in sales.
